If we consider each parallelogram $ABCD$ has vertices $A (2,3)$, $B (6,5)$, $C (8,9)$, and $D (4,7)$. A point $E (x, y)$ inside it makes four small triangles $AEB$, $AEC$, $BED$, and $CED$ having equal perimeters. 

We have $AEB + AEC + BED + CED = Perimeter (ABCD)$. This can be achieved if the sum of the perimeters of any three of these should add to the perimeter of the parallelogram $BCDA$. This sums up to $6\sqrt{5} + 2\sqrt{5} + 2\sqrt{5} + 6\sqrt{5} = 20\sqrt{5}$, because  $BCDC = 6\sqrt{5}$. Therefore, the length of the perimeter each triangle $AEB, AEC, BED, CED$ should be $(20\sqrt{5})/4 = 5\sqrt{5}$.

Using geometry and concepts related to parallel line properties and also using distance formula we will calculate coordinates of $E$. 

The resulting coordinates of $E$ will be checked and ultimately the values will be used in  $5x + 2y$.

Thus the value of  $5x + 2y$ = (when $E$ coordinates are calculated)
